insights.headline: Gold eases to $4,014 as a firmer dollar meets Fed week; silver slips below $54 to near 11-month lows
insights.summary: Gold edged lower in Asian trade on Tuesday to $4,013.70 an ounce as a firmer dollar weighed, with the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting and Thursday's PCE inflation data ahead; markets price about an 11% chance of a hike this week and 82% for December. Silver slipped below $54 to about $53.80, near Monday's 11-month low of $53.01. In India, the wholesale gold discount has narrowed to $6-8 an ounce from $66 in September, and the rupee closed at 95.1850 per dollar for a third straight weaker session.
points: Spot gold eased 0.1% to $4,013.70 in early Asian trade Tuesday as a firmer dollar weighed ahead of the Fed meeting.
Silver slipped below $54 to about $53.80, near Monday's 11-month low of $53.01, FXStreet reports.
Markets price about an 11% chance of a Fed hike this week and 82% for December, per CME FedWatch via Reuters.
India's wholesale gold discount narrowed to $6-8/oz from $66 in September as festive restocking absorbed supply.
The rupee closed at 95.1850 per dollar on Monday, its third straight weaker session, lifting landed import costs.

trending.title: Fed week takes charge
trending.summary: Gold's Tuesday easing keeps the Fed's October 27-28 meeting at the centre of the market, with a firmer dollar and December hike bets capping the recovery as easing oil prices trim inflation worries.

trending.title: Silver tests 11-month lows
trending.summary: Silver's slide below $54 extends a deep correction from its January peak, with bearish technical signals, growing COMEX shorts and a $48.29 support level now framing the debate.

trending.title: Dhanteras demand meets a thinner discount
trending.summary: Festive restocking has nearly erased the wholesale discount Indian buyers enjoyed in September, while the World Gold Council links US midterm scenarios to Dhanteras demand.

trending.title: A weaker rupee adds to the landed cost
trending.summary: The rupee's third straight weaker session compounds the vanished import discount for Indian buyers, even as MCX futures steadied after last week's sell-off.

items.title: Gold eases as stronger dollar weighs, Fed meeting in focus
items.summary: Spot gold edged 0.1% lower to $4,013.70 an ounce in early Asian trade on Tuesday as a firmer dollar weighed on dollar-priced bullion, Reuters reports via the Economic Times, while December futures slipped 0.3% to $4,027.10. Traders await the Fed's October 27-28 meeting and Thursday's PCE data, pricing about an 11% chance of a hike this week and 82% for December.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD falls toward 11-month lows after slipping below $54.00
items.summary: Silver slipped below $54 in Asian trade on Tuesday, trading around $53.80 an ounce after minor gains the previous day, FXStreet reports, near an 11-month low of $53.01 recorded on Monday. Elevated energy prices keep inflation risks in focus and sustain expectations of further tightening, though easing oil and bargain-hunting ahead of the Fed decision could cushion the fall.

items.title: Gold holds above $4,000 as Hormuz diplomacy cools crude ahead of Fed decision - Kitco PM Report
items.summary: Spot gold climbed back above $4,000 an ounce in late US trading on Monday as easing crude prices softened inflation worries ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting, with diplomatic efforts involving Iran and regional powers trimming the geopolitical premium in oil. Silver held above $54, but Kitco notes both metals remain exposed to Treasury yields, the dollar and the rate outlook.

items.title: Gold's Import Discount Dropped to $8/oz: Dhanteras 2026 Math
items.summary: Citing World Gold Council data, OneMint reports the discount at which Indian wholesale gold traded to its landed import cost shrank from a September average of $66 an ounce to $6-8 an ounce by mid-October, as festive restocking ahead of Dhanteras on November 6 absorbed supply. With the cushion nearly gone, buyers face the full 15% import duty and a weaker rupee.

MCX gold December futures opened ₹277 higher at ₹1,42,301 per 10 grams on Monday and traded at ₹1,42,500, up 0.34%, after last week's near-4% slide, while silver December futures traded at ₹1,95,572 per kg after an intraday high of ₹1,97,186. Experts cited by IANS said gold needs to reclaim ₹1,43,000-₹1,43,700 to stabilise, with silver facing resistance at ₹2,00,000-₹2,02,000.
items.title: Gold, silver bounce back after sharp sell-off, but yellow metal near 3-month low
Inflows into gold ETFs turned negative after 13 weeks as the yellow metal fell 4% last week
items.summary: Physically backed gold ETFs saw net outflows last week for the first time in 13 weeks, World Gold Council data show, with investors redeeming $3.01 billion against $1.80 billion of inflows as gold fell nearly 4% in its worst week since June. US investors led the redemptions at $1.7 billion, with the Fed's October 27-28 meeting now the key near-term driver.

items.title: Rupee weakens for third session as importers step up dollar bids, foreign outflows bite
items.summary: The rupee closed at 95.1850 per dollar on Monday, down 0.3% on the day and about 0.8% over three sessions, as importer dollar demand, Brent crude near $115 a barrel and foreign outflows weighed. Traders noted the absence of recent RBI dollar sales that had supported the currency; a weaker rupee raises the landed cost of dollar-priced bullion for Indian buyers.

items.title: Digital gold purchases surge 83% to Rs 2,590 crore in September
items.summary: Citing World Gold Council data, the Economic Times reports Indian digital gold purchases rose to Rs 2,590 crore in September, up 83% from a year earlier and 4% from August, with volumes of 1.7 tonnes. The firm demand, attributed to low minimum investments and easy access, came even as physical buying stayed selective ahead of Dhanteras.

items.title: Silver (XAG/USD) Price Forecast: Bearish Signals Put $48.29 Support in Focus
items.summary: FXEmpire's technical read keeps silver in a bearish structure after its fall from the January peak of $121.67, with the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement at $48.29 now in focus as a potentially significant support level inside a late-2025 consolidation range of $54.49 to $45.55. Short-term oversold conditions could produce a bounce, but rallies face selling pressure until momentum turns.

items.title: Silver crashes 53% from 2026 peak, gold falls 26%
items.summary: Silver has fallen more than 53% from its January 2026 record near $117 an ounce to around $54 by October 23, as Middle East tensions and persistent inflation weighed on bullion. Gold has also dropped 26% from its all-time peak, leaving festive buyers facing a very different market from January's highs.

items.title: Silver Below $55 as COMEX Shorts Outpace New Longs
items.summary: Silver trades below $55 as COMEX shorts rise faster than longs, increasing breakdown risk ahead of the Fed decision despite easing real yields. CFTC data published October 23, for positions as of October 20, show managed-money longs up 378 contracts to 16,180 while shorts rose 2,492 to 12,675, cutting the net long to 3,505 from 5,619 a week earlier.

items.title: Gold prices squeezed between rising oil and falling yields, Fresnillo silver output declines in 2026 – Heraeus
items.summary: Heraeus analysts say gold is caught between rising oil prices, with Brent back above $110 a barrel after renewed Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, and falling Treasury yields, the 10-year yield retreating toward 5.0% from about 5.35% earlier in October. The firm also notes output at Fresnillo, the world's largest primary silver producer, slid over the first three quarters of 2026.

items.title: Gold Reclaims $4000 as Data Show Modest Speculative Retreat Before Latest Sell-Off
items.summary: Spot gold traded at $4,021 an ounce by Monday lunchtime, up 0.2% from Friday's London PM auction, after falling 4.2% last week to $4,013 at Friday's fix. BullionVault notes eight straight weeks of declines in speculative net longs in Comex gold futures and options, a modest retreat relative to the price fall; silver traded at $54.15, up 0.5%, after a 6.6% weekly fall.

items.title: Dhanteras, Diwali 2026: 4 factors that could affect gold prices after US midterm elections, according to WGC
items.summary: The World Gold Council examines how the US midterm elections could affect gold, Upstox reports: a Democratic-controlled Congress could make policymaking less predictable, pushing the administration toward wider use of executive orders, which the Council's Juan Carlos Artigas says could raise risk premia and support gold. Indian seasonal demand is gathering pace as retailers restock.

items.title: Why is gold price under pressure ahead of Dhanteras, Diwali? What should interested buyers do? Experts's views, target
items.summary: Mint examines why gold is under pressure ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali, with experts linking the pullback to a stronger dollar, elevated bond yields and oil-driven inflation worries ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting. The metal's weekly fall left MCX gold near ₹1.42 lakh per 10 grams as festive buying approaches.

items.bis_insight_sentence: BIS extended mandatory gold hallmarking to 12 more districts, taking coverage to 392 districts.
items.bis_point: BIS extended mandatory gold hallmarking to 12 more districts, taking coverage to 392 districts across 26 states and union territories.
items.summary: BIS has extended mandatory hallmarking of gold jewellery to 12 more districts under the Third Amendment Order, 2026, issued on August 3, The Retail Jeweller India reports. Coverage rises from 380 to 392 districts across 26 states and union territories, including Kancheepuram, Panipat, Angul and Jhargram — a purity check for festive jewellery buyers.
items.title: BIS expands mandatory hallmarkingof gold jewellery to 12 more districts
5 things happening in the gold market ahead of Diwali and Dhanteras 2026, as per WGC
items.summary: The World Gold Council's latest India update, 'Seasonal demand shows early strength', says prices steadied after September's sharp fall and domestic discounts narrowed from $66 an ounce in September to $8 by October 16 as festive and wedding-season demand built. Demand is strengthening into Diwali and Dhanteras, though the Council cautions high prices may still cap volumes.

items.title: Senco Gold to acquire 68% stake in August Jewellery for ₹68 crore
items.summary: Senco Gold has signed definitive agreements to buy a 68% stake in August Jewellery, the company behind online jewellery brand Melorra, for ₹68 crore in tranches. With a promoter-group entity also investing, the total holding will reach 79% and August Jewellery will become a Senco subsidiary, with completion targeted by February 2027.

items.title: What are different ways to invest in gold this Dhanteras?
items.summary: Indian households buying gold for Dhanteras and Diwali can choose physical gold, gold ETFs, gold mutual funds, digital gold or electronic gold receipts, with sovereign gold bonds another route. Each form differs on storage, liquidity and cost, so the right choice depends on whether the metal is for wearing, gifting or investing.
